Set control parameters for gcTMB

Source: R/gcTMBcontrol.R
gcTMBcontrol.Rd

Set control parameters for gcTMB

Usage

gcTMBcontrol(
  optimiser = "nlminb",
  iter.max = 1000,
  eval.max = 2000,
  smallsample = TRUE,
  sdreport = TRUE,
  restart = FALSE,
  onerror = c("stop", "warning")
)

Arguments

optimiser

Character string. The optimiser: only "nlminb" (nlminb, with the gradients of TMB) is available, for the fit, the profiles and the bootstrap.

iter.max

Integer. Maximum number of iterations of the optimiser, see nlminb.

eval.max

Integer. Maximum number of evaluations of the objective function, see nlminb.

smallsample

Logical. If TRUE (default), gaussian and lognormal models without random effects, without autocorrelation and without a variance function use the unbiased residual variance with n - p residual degrees of freedom and t quantiles, as lm and nls; if FALSE, the maximum likelihood estimate and normal quantiles. See gcTMB.

sdreport

Logical. If TRUE (default), the fit computes the covariance matrix of the estimates (TMB's sdreport), for standard errors, Wald intervals and the standard errors of predictions. FALSE skips it, which saves about a quarter of the time of a fit with random effects, e.g. in simulation studies that only need the estimates and the log-likelihood: the standard errors, vcov and the Wald intervals are then NA, and converged does not check the Hessian. Profile and bootstrap intervals are still available.

restart

Logical. If TRUE, a fit whose optimiser does not report convergence, or whose largest absolute gradient is above 1e-3, is optimised once more from its estimates, and keeps the better of the two optima. With few groups and several correlated random effects, the likelihood is often so flat in some directions that nlminb reports "singular convergence" or "false convergence", or stops with a gradient slightly above the tolerance, at the maximum: the restart then hardly changes the log-likelihood. The improvement of the log-likelihood by the restart is kept in the fit (fit$restart$improvement), and converged accepts a fit that the restart improved by less than its argument lltol. FALSE (default) for no restart.

onerror

Character string. What a fit does when the fitting itself fails with an error, e.g. the optimiser stops at a point where the likelihood cannot be evaluated, or the covariance of the estimates (sdreport) cannot be computed: "stop" (default) stops with the error, as before; "warning" turns the error into a warning and returns the gcTMB object, so that a loop over many fits, e.g. a simulation study, keeps the failed ones. If the optimiser fails, the returned object has the starting values as its estimates (or the optimum before a failed refinement); if only sdreport fails, it has the estimates without standard errors, as with sdreport=FALSE. The error message is kept in fit$fiterror, printed by print and summary, and converged reports the fit as not converged. Errors in the specification of the model (formulas, data, links, starting values) stop in either case.

Value

A list with the control parameters.

Examples

gcTMBcontrol(iter.max=2000)
#> $optimiser
#> [1] "nlminb"
#> 
#> $iter.max
#> [1] 2000
#> 
#> $eval.max
#> [1] 2000
#> 
#> $smallsample
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $sdreport
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $restart
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $onerror
#> [1] "stop"
#> 
# small-sample inference switched off: maximum likelihood estimate of the residual sd
gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, data=FabaHeights25, control=list(smallsample=FALSE))
#> Call:
#> gcTMB(form = Height ~ DAS, data = FabaHeights25, control = list(smallsample = FALSE))
#> 
#> Model:  logistic, truncated at b4 = 0
#> Family: gaussian, identity link for all parameters
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#> b1:(Intercept)  b2:(Intercept)  b3:(Intercept)  
#>         120.79           30.73           12.88  
#> 
#> Residual standard deviation: 7.982
# estimates only, without standard errors
gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, rform=b1 ~ 1 | Plant_ID, data=FabaHeights25, control=list(sdreport=FALSE))
#> Call:
#> gcTMB(form = Height ~ DAS, rform = b1 ~ 1 | Plant_ID, data = FabaHeights25, 
#>     control = list(sdreport = FALSE))
#> 
#> Model:  logistic, truncated at b4 = 0
#> Family: gaussian, identity link for all parameters
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#> b1:(Intercept)  b2:(Intercept)  b3:(Intercept)  
#>         120.56           30.61           12.89  
#> 
#> Random effects:
#>  Groups   Name Std.Dev.
#>  Plant_ID b1   11.85   
#> 
#> Residual standard deviation: 3.127
# a second optimisation from the estimates when the first one does not converge
fit <- gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, rform=b1 + b2 + b3 ~ 1 | Plant_ID, data=FabaHeights25,
             control=list(restart=TRUE))
converged(fit)
#> [1] TRUE
# a loop over models: a fit that fails is returned with a warning instead of stopping the loop
fits <- lapply(c("logistic", "gompertz"), function(m)
  gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, data=FabaHeights25, model=m, control=list(onerror="warning")))
# the error of each fit, NULL if it did not fail
lapply(fits, function(f) f$fiterror)
#> [[1]]
#> NULL
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> NULL
#>
